question: Which welding process uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode and an inert shielding gas to produce high-quality welds on non-ferrous metals?
options: Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW)
Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)
Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)
Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)

question: When performing a tensile test on a welded joint, which property is being measured?
options: The hardness of the heat-affected zone
The maximum stress the weld can withstand before fracture
The ductility of the base metal only
The impact resistance of the weld at low temperatures

question: In pipe welding, the 6G position refers to which configuration?
options: Pipe in the horizontal fixed position
Pipe in the vertical fixed position
Pipe inclined at 45 degrees in a fixed position
Pipe in the flat position rotated continuously

question: What is the primary purpose of preheating a high-carbon steel workpiece before welding?
options: To increase the tensile strength of the weld metal
To reduce the risk of hydrogen-induced cracking in the heat-affected zone
To improve the electrical conductivity of the base metal
To increase the deposition rate of the filler material

question: Which type of weld discontinuity is characterized by fusion that does not extend to the full cross-section of the weld joint or fuses with the base metal?
options: Porosity
Undercut
Incomplete fusion
Overlap

question: According to the AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code, what is the maximum permissible undercut depth for a statically loaded structural member?
options: 1/32 inch (0.8 mm)
1/16 inch (1.6 mm)
3/32 inch (2.4 mm)
1/8 inch (3.2 mm)

question: In MIG/GMAW welding, the term 'spray transfer' mode is best achieved with which combination of parameters?
options: Low voltage, low wire feed speed, and 100% CO2 shielding gas
High voltage, high wire feed speed, and argon-rich shielding gas above the transition current
Low voltage, pulsed current, and 75% argon/25% CO2 shielding gas
Medium voltage, medium amperage, and 100% helium shielding gas

question: What does the term 'interpass temperature' refer to in multi-pass welding?
options: The temperature of the base metal before the first weld pass
The maximum temperature measured between successive weld passes
The temperature at which post-weld heat treatment begins
The temperature used to calibrate the welding machine thermocouple

question: Which non-destructive testing (NDT) method is most effective for detecting subsurface discontinuities such as internal porosity or inclusions in a weld?
options: Liquid penetrant testing (PT)
Visual inspection (VT)
Radiographic testing (RT)
Magnetic particle testing (MT)

question: When reading a welding symbol on an engineering drawing, where is the reference line located and what does the arrow side indicate?
options: The reference line is a vertical line; the arrow side indicates the weld is on the opposite side of the joint
The reference line is a horizontal line; the arrow side indicates the side of the joint where the weld symbol is placed
The reference line is a dashed line; the arrow side indicates a groove weld only
The reference line is a diagonal line; the arrow side indicates the welding process to be used

question: What is the correct procedure when a welder discovers a crack in a previously completed weld during inspection?
options: Weld directly over the crack to fill it with new weld metal
Grind or gouge out the crack completely beyond its ends and re-weld following the approved WPS
Apply weld peening to close the crack and continue with the next pass
Apply a cold repair epoxy compound rated for structural applications

question: In plasma arc cutting (PAC), what role does the plasma gas play in the cutting process?
options: It acts solely as a shielding medium to prevent oxidation of the cut edge
It is ionized to form a high-temperature, high-velocity jet that melts and removes the base metal
It provides the electrical current needed to maintain the arc
It cools the torch nozzle and prevents electrode erosion

question: Which heat treatment process is applied after welding to relieve residual stresses in a fabricated steel structure?
options: Annealing
Normalizing
Post-Weld Heat Treatment (PWHT) / Stress Relief
Case hardening

question: When fabricating a T-joint with a fillet weld, the throat of the fillet weld is defined as which measurement?
options: The length along the face of the weld from toe to toe
The perpendicular distance from the root of the joint to the hypotenuse of the largest right triangle that can be inscribed within the weld cross-section
The distance from the surface of one member to the surface of the other member
The total width of the heat-affected zone on both base metal members

question: A Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) is qualified by which document that records the actual variables used during a qualification test?
options: Welder Performance Qualification Record (WPQR)
Procedure Qualification Record (PQR)
Material Test Report (MTR)
Inspection and Test Plan (ITP)
